speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of chorioamnionitis, low Apgar scores, and new-onset seizures, neonatal meningitis is highly suspected. REQUEST TEST: Lumbar Puncture with CSF analysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: With a normal CSF analysis effectively ruling out meningitis, we must consider other causes of neonatal seizures in the context of chorioamnionitis and prematurity, such as hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy or metabolic disturbances. I will now request a blood gas analysis and serum glucose levels to assess for acidosis or hypoglycemia, along with a head ultrasound to check for intracranial hemorrhage.
